page: Amazon Web Services r7i.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8488C processor with an x86_64 architecture, providing 4 virtual CPUs across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading running at 3.2 GHz. The CPU includes a 105 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for matrix math acceleration. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPUs, and has a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates a divergence between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the average category. Geekbench text processing shows strong performance. However, multi-core benchmarks, including stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, fall into the lower 25th percentile. Memory bandwidth tests for both small cached blocks and large uncached blocks also register in the lower tier, alongside database operations and Redis SET performance.

The r7i.xlarge offers a high-density DDR5 memory configuration relative to its compute footprint, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound workloads that do not require high parallel compute scaling. The presence of AMX instructions provides specialized acceleration for small-scale deep learning tasks, as evidenced by average-tier LLM inference speeds on small and medium models. This instance is suited for memory-intensive applications with moderate CPU requirements, such as text processing, caching layers, and lightweight web serving, though it is less optimal for highly parallelized database operations or heavy multi-threaded compilation.
